ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p293#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p293#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p293#2/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the earth's adornment as its vegetation sprouting and becoming beautiful.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p293#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوه تعالى ﴿ وازينت ﴾ قال أنبتت وحسنت

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p293#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p293#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p293#2/r2.claim: He explains that the garden seemed not to have flourished the previous day.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p293#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ كأن لم تغن بالأمس ﴾ قال كأن لم تنعم بالأمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r1.claim: Following the warning that people’s transgression harms themselves, the parable reminds them how quickly worldly life disappears after it delights them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r1.anchor: ضرب مثلا عجيبا غريبا للحياة الدنيا تذكر من يبغي فيها على سرعة زوالها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls this a compound simile: the world’s rapid decline after its flourishing resembles lush vegetation becoming dry debris.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r2.anchor: هذا من التشبيه المركب، شبهت حال الدنيا في سرعة تقضيها وانقراض نعيمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r3.claim: ‘Only’ is not restrictive here, in either lexical meaning or usage, because the Qur’an gives other parables for worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r3.anchor: وإنما هنا ليست للحصر لا وضعا ولا استعمالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r4.claim: ‘Parable’ may mean a description or a proverbial comparison; the apparent image compares worldly life with water in what it enables and how its benefit ends.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r4.anchor: والمثل هنا يحتمل أن يراد به الصفة، وأن يراد به القول السائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r5.claim: Other parses compare worldly life to vegetation nourished by water, with a deleted noun, or to people’s life renewed by rain; the phrase about its owners thinking they can control it supports the latter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r5.anchor: وقيل: شبهت الحياة الدنيا بالنبات على تلك الأوصاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r6.claim: ‘The sky’ may refer to clouds or to the direction of the sky; the apparent reading is that vegetation mingled with rain by clinging to and taking it as nourishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r6.anchor: والسماء إما أن يراد من السحاب، وإما أن يراد من جهة السماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r7.claim: The bāʾ can indicate accompaniment: each of two things can be said to mix with the other, and the rain nourishes every part of the plant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r7.anchor: وكل مختلطين يصح في كل منهما أن يقال: اختلط بصاحبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r8.speaker: الكرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r8.claim: Al-Kirmānī takes the mixing as adjacency, since mixture ordinarily involves interpenetration; Abū Ḥayyān says interpenetration itself is possible and need not be reduced to adjacency.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r8.anchor: وقال الكرماني: فاختلط به اختلاط مجاورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r9.claim: He considers ‘varied,’ ‘composed,’ and ‘extended’ possible suggested senses of the verb, but says the wording does not support ‘varied.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p36/r9.anchor: وقيل: اختلط اختلف وتنوع بالماء، وينبو لفظ اختلط عن هذا التفسير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reads the plants as interwoven with one another because of the water; on this reading the preposition marks cause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وصلت فرقة النبات بقوله فاختلظ أي: اختلط النبات بعضه ببعض بسبب الماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r2.claim: The alternative making water the subject of “mixed” and pausing there is syntactically weak; the pause breaks connected, eloquent speech into obscure, uninformative wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r2.anchor: لأنه تفكيك للكلام المتصل الصحيح المعنى، الفصيح اللفظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r3.claim: The named foods distinguish edible plants: people eat grains, fruits, and vegetables, while livestock eat grass and other pasture.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r3.anchor: بين أن المراد أحد القسمين بمن فقال: مما يأكل الناس، كالحبوب والثمار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r4.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r4.claim: Al-Ḥūfī attaches min to ikhtalaṭa; Abū al-Baqāʾ instead makes the phrase a circumstantial modifier of the plants, which Abū Ḥayyān regards as the clearer parse, with an omitted copula.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r5.claim: The temporal particle ḥattā requires a preceding action that continues; supply continued growth, or understand ikhtalaṭa as the plants remaining mixed with water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p37/r5.anchor: وحتى غاية، فيحتاج أن يكون الفعل الذي قبلها متطاولا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r1.claim: The adornment is supplied by the plants, including their grains, fruits, and flowers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r1.anchor: بنباتها وما أودع فيه من الحبوب والثمار والأزهار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r2.claim: Wa-izzayyanat may repeat the idea of taking adornment, or add that the land deliberately adorned itself; attributing both actions to the land is a fine metaphor.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r3.speaker: قراء الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r3.claim: The common reading assimilates the t of underlying watazayyanat into z and adds a connecting hamza because assimilation leaves z unvocalized.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وازينت وأصله وتزينت، فأدغمت التاء في الزاي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r4.speaker: أبي وعبد الله وزيد بن علي والأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r4.claim: These readers have the unassimilated form wa-tazayyanat on the tafaʿʿalat pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعبد الله، وزيد بن علي، والأعمش: وتزينت على وزن تفعلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r5.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وأبو عبد الرحمن وابن يعمر والحسن والشعبي وأبو العالية وقتادة ونصر بن عاصم وابن هرمز وعيسى الثقفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r5.claim: This group reads wa-azyanat on the afʿalat pattern, meaning its adornment appeared or came due; the preserved yāʾ is rare, with azānat the expected form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r5.anchor: وقرأ سعد بن أبي وقاص، وأبو عبد الرحمن، وابن يعمر، والحسن، والشعبي، وأبو العالية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r6.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r6.claim: Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī is reported with an open hamza in an unusual ifʿaʾallat form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عثمان النهدي بهمزة مفتوحة بوزن افعألت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the related group reading a dialect and cites poetry as evidence; the elders of ʿAwf b. Abī Jamīla have a reading with doubled n, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya identifies with Abū ʿUthmān’s.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r7.anchor: ونسب ابن عطية هذه القراءة لفرقة فقال: وقرأت فرقة وازيأنت وهي لغة منها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r8.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r8.claim: Another group reads wa-zāyanat, from an assimilated original watazāyanat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r8.anchor: وقرأت فرقة: وازاينت، والأصل وتزاينت فأدغم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r9.claim: Here ẓann has its ordinary sense of judging one possibility more likely; the proposed sense “they became certain” is unsound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r9.anchor: والظن هنا على بابه من ترجيح أحد الجائزين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r10.claim: Being able to manage the land means being able to harvest its crop, benefit from it, and obtain its yield, made possible by healthy growth free from blight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r10.anchor: ومعنى القدرة عليها التمكن من تحصيلها ومنفعتها ورفع غلتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r11.claim: The pronoun in ahluhā refers to the land, with an omitted noun meaning its crop’s people; readings that make it refer to the yield or adornment are weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r11.anchor: والضمير في أهلها عائد على الأرض، وهو على حذف مضاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r12.claim: The answer to idhā is “Our command came”; the command may be wind, cold or hot winds, mice, locusts, or another destructive calamity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r12.anchor: وجواب إذا قوله: أتاها أمرنا كالريح والصر والسموم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r13.claim: An alternative takes “Our command came” to mean that God’s command to destroy the crop arrived.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r14.claim: The night-or-day wording either leaves the time unstated though God knows it, or distributes events: some lands are struck at night, others by day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p38/r14.anchor: وأبهم في قوله: ليلا أو نهارا، وقد علم تعالى متى يأتيها أمره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r1.claim: Ḥaṣīd is a passive sense meaning harvested; Abū ʿUbayda glosses it as cut off. Calling blighted crops “harvested” is metaphorical, or an implicit simile for harvested grain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r1.anchor: والحصيد: فعيل بمعنى مفعول أي: المحصود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains ḥaṣīd as completely uprooted or cut off.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r3.claim: “As if it had not flourished yesterday” intensifies devastation: the land seems never to have existed or displayed its pleasing green abundance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r3.anchor: مبالغة في التلف والهلاك حتى كأنها لم توجد قبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r4.claim: Ḥasan and Qatāda read the verb with masculine agreement; the antecedent may be the omitted crop or adornment, but Abū Ḥayyān prefers the harvested crop.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة: كأن لم يغن بالياء على التذكير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r5.speaker: مروان بن الحكم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r5.claim: Marwān b. al-Ḥakam reportedly read tataġannā with two tāʾs; al-Aʿshā’s verse supports taghannī from ġaniya, “to dwell.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r5.anchor: وكان مروان بن الحكم يقرأ على المنبر: كأن لم تتغن بتاءين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī’s equation of yesterday with any time or with “just now”: the phrase means it seemed not to have existed in past time, emphasizing its rapid disappearance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r6.anchor: وليس الأمس عبارة عن مطلق الوقت، ولا هو مرادف كقوله: آنفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r7.claim: A report about Ubayy’s codex adds that God would not destroy the land except for its people’s sins; another transmitted wording names God explicitly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r7.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي: كأن لم تغن بالأمس، وما كنا لنهلكها إلا بذنوب أهلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r8.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r8.claim: Abū Salama reportedly read in Ubayy’s reading that the land was destroyed only for its people’s sins; Abū Ḥayyān says this should not be recited because it departs from the agreed codex script.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p39/r8.anchor: وكان أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن يقرأ في قراءة أبي كأن لم تغن بالأمس، وما أهلكناها

AKHFASH:v1p371/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p371/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p371/r2.claim: كماء means like the likeness of water, with مثل understood.

AKHFASH:v1p371/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p371/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p371/r3.claim: وازينت represents وتزينت: tāʾ assimilates into the nearby zāy, then a connecting alif is added because the word cannot begin with a still consonant; the heavy form reflects the same source.
AKHFASH:v1p371/r3.anchor: يريد "وتزينت" ولكن أدغم التاء في الزاي لقرب المخرجين

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r1.claim: Rain makes the land grow plants, which become mixed and joined to one another.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r1.anchor: {فاختلط به نبات الأرض} يريد أن الأرض أنبتت بنزول المطر فاختلط النبات بالمطر، واتصل كل واحد بصاحبه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r2.claim: The land takes its adornment in plants; zakhraf originally means gold and extends to patterns, light, flowers, and anything decorative.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r2.anchor: {حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها} أي: زينتها بالنبات. وأصل الزخرف: الذهب. ثم يقال للنقش وللنور والزهر وكل شيء زين: زخرف.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r3.claim: The land's owners think they can control what it has grown, its grain and fruit.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r3.anchor: {وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها} أي: [على] ما أنبتته من حب وثمر.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r4.claim: Lam taghn means the land had not been inhabited the previous day; maghānī are dwellings and ghanā means to reside.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p195#3/r4.anchor: {كأن لم تغن بالأمس} أي: كأن لم تكن عامرة بالأمس. والمغاني المنازل. واحدها مغنى. وغنيت بالمكان: إذا أقمت به.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r1.claim: The opening simile introduces the fleeting enjoyment of worldly life and the rapid disappearance of its pleasures after people are drawn in by its flourishing.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r1.anchor: كلام مستأنف لبيان شأن الحياة الدنيا وقصر مدة التمتع فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r2.claim: A parable transfers an unusual or wondrous matter from its source to what it illustrates; here the comparison depicts worldly life quickly passing away.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r2.anchor: وأصل المثل ما شبه مضربه بمورده يستعار للأمر العجيب المستغرب

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r3.claim: The water causes the earth's vegetation to grow densely and intertwine; Ibn ʿAbbās's explanation supports this causal reading, though others take the water as accompanying the vegetation.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r3.anchor: فالباء للسببية ومنهممن أبقاها على المصاحبة وجعل الإختلاط بالماء نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r4.claim: The phrase about what people and livestock eat is circumstantial and refers to crops, vegetables, grasses, and pasture.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r4.anchor: كالبقول والزروع والحشيش والمراعي والجار والمجرور في موضع الحال من النبات

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r5.claim: Several commentators construe the adorned earth as a bride: the bride is an implied metaphor, taking adornment is its imaginative completion, and the following wording extends it.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r5.anchor: ذكر غير واحد أن في الكلام إستعارة بالكناية حيث شبهت الأرض بالعروس

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r6.claim: Another explanation takes the earth's adornment as gold, metaphorically describing its freshness and pleasing appearance.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : الزخرف الذهب أستعير للنضارة والمنظر الشار

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r7.claim: The standard form derives from tazayyanat by assimilation of tāʾ into zāy and an added connecting hamza; several variant readings preserve or reshape the form.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r7.anchor: وأصل ازينت تزينت فأدغمت التاء في الزاي وسكنت فإجتلبت همزة وصل

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r8.speaker: عبدالله
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r8.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads the underlying form تزينت before assimilation.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r9.speaker: الأعرج والشعبي وأبو العالية ونصر بن عاصم والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r9.claim: These readers, with disagreement from al-Ḥasan, transmit the form أرينت on the pattern of afʿalat.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج والشعبي وأبو العالية ونصر بن عاصم والحسن بخلاف ( وأرينت ) بوزن أفعلت

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r10.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r10.claim: Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī reads ازيأنت with a hamza after the initial connecting hamza.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو عثمان النهدي ( ازيأنت ) بهمزة وصل بعدها زاي ساكنة

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r11.speaker: عوف بن جميل
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r11.claim: ʿAwf ibn Jamīl reads ازيانت without replacing the alif with hamza; another reading intensifies the form as ازاينت.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ عوف بن جميل ( ازيانت ) بألف من غير إبدال وقريء ( ازاينت ) لقصد المبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r12.claim: The verbal forms here indicate becoming adorned, either by acquiring beauty or by adorning oneself.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r12.anchor: ومعنى الأفعال هنال هنا الصيرورة أي صارت ذات زينة أو صيرت نفسها كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r13.claim: The owners think they can use the earth, obtain its fruit, and harvest its yields; the coming divine command then strikes its crops with destructive calamities.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p100#2/r13.anchor: والمراد ظنوا أنهم متمكنون من منفعتها محصلون لثمرتهارافعون لغلتها

ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r1.claim: The punishment can arrive by night or day: neither their heedlessness nor their wakefulness prevents it, and no defender can avert it.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r1.anchor: لا فرق في إتيان العذاب بين زمن غفلتهم وزمن يقظتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r2.claim: The harvested field is an explicit simile for the ruined vegetation; a direct metaphor is also possible, but al-Sakkākī's implied metaphor in which the embellished earth is the thriving plant is remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا من التشبيه لذكر الطرفين فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r3.speaker: السكّاكي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r3.claim: Al-Sakkākī reads the passage as an implied metaphor, with the harvest image functioning as imaginative elaboration; al-Ālūsī finds this reading strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r3.anchor: وذهب السكاكي إلى أن في الكلام إستعارة بالكناية

ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r4.claim: The verb تغن means that the plant did not remain or dwell there; the omitted possessive makes the earth itself seem harvested and then unchanged, intensifying the image.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r4.anchor: أي لم يمكث ولم يقم فتغن من غني بالمكان إذا أقام ومكث فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r5.claim: The pronouns are best referred throughout to the earth, with ellipsis; on al-Ḥasan's masculine reading يغني, however, the subject must be vegetation or crops.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r5.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن إرجاع الضمائر كلها للأرض ولومع إرتكاب التجوز في الإسناد أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r6.claim: Yesterday is an idiom for a recent time before the event; the simile can be circumstantial or an independent answer to an implied question.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r6.anchor: أي فيما قبل إتيان أمرنا بزمان قريب فإن الأمس مثل في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r7.claim: The composite comparison is the sudden disappearance of lush, intertwined vegetation after people expect it to escape disaster, not the rain itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r7.anchor: والممثل به في الآية ما يفهم من الكلام وهو زوال خضرة النبات فجأة

ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r8.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r8.claim: A reading attributed to Ubayy adds that God destroyed the land only because of its people's sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r8.anchor: وعن أبي أنه قرأ ( كأن لم تغن بالأمس وما أهلكناها إلا بذنوب أهلها )

ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r9.claim: The verses being set out are Quranic signs, which are clarified for reflective people because they benefit from them; alternatively, the signs are the created events in the parable.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r9.anchor: وعن أبي مجلز أنه قال : كان مكتوبا إلى جنب هذه الآية فمحي

ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r10.speaker: أبو مجلز
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r10.claim: Abū Mijlaz says a saying about Adam's child wanting a third valley of wealth and being filled only by earth was written beside this verse, then erased.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r10.anchor: كان مكتوبا إلى جنب هذه الآية فمحي ( ولو أن لإبن آدم واديين من مال لتمنى واديا ثالثا

ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r11.claim: The pronoun in the claim that the owners could control it is understood as the earth; alternative referents are crops, fruit, or adornment.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p101/r11.anchor: الكناية للزروع وقيل : للثمرة وقيل : للزينة لإنفهام ذلك من الكلام

MAJAZ:v1p276/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p276/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p276/r4.claim: Ḥaṣīdan means cut down from the root; here the singular form carries the collective sense of all the crops.
MAJAZ:v1p276/r4.anchor: «فجعلناها حصيدا» (24) اى مستأصلين، والحصيد من الزرع والنبات المجذوذ من أصله

MAJAZ:v1p276/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p276/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p276/r5.claim: The word ḥaṣīd may also refer collectively to crops, while ḥaṣāʾid names harvested plants.
MAJAZ:v1p276/r5.anchor: وهو يقع أيضا لفظه على لفظ الجميع من الزرع والنبات فجاء فى هذه الآية على معنى الجميع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r1.claim: The parable describes worldly life’s passing away and disappearance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا} في فنائها وزوالها، {كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says rain produces plants in many colors; people eat grains and fruits, while livestock eat grass.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r2.anchor: أي: بالمطر، {نبات الأرض} قال ابن عباس: نبت بالماء من كل لون، {مما يأكل الناس} من الحبوب والثمار، {والأنعام} من الحشيش،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r3.claim: The earth takes on beauty as blossoms appear in green, red, yellow, and white.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r3.anchor: {حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها} حسنها وبهجتها، وظهر الزهر أخضر وأحمر وأصفر وأبيض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r4.claim: The phrase means the earth adorned itself; Ibn Masud’s reading explicitly has تزينت.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r4.anchor: {وازينت} أي: تزينت، وكذلك هي في قراءة ابن مسعود: "تزينت".

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r5.claim: The pronoun in capable of harvesting it refers grammatically to the earth, while its intended referent is the vegetation; other views refer it to the crop or adornment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r5.anchor: {وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها} على جذاذها وقطافها وحصادها، رد الكناية إلى الأرض. والمراد: النبات إذ كان مفهوما، وقيل: ردها إلى الغلة. وقيل: إلى الزينة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r6.claim: God’s command is His decree to destroy the crop, leaving it cut down as though it had not existed the day before.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r6.anchor: {أتاها أمرنا} قضاؤنا، بإهلاكها، {ليلا أو نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا} أي: محصودة مقطوعة، {كأن لم تغن بالأمس} كأن لم تكن بالأمس،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r7.claim: Qatada says God’s punishment reaches a person attached to worldly life when he is most heedless.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p128#2/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: معناه أن المتشبث بالدنيا يأتيه أمر الله وعذابه أغفل ما يكون.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r1.claim: The parable captures worldly life: it passes quickly, and its pleasures vanish after people become attached and deceived by it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r1.anchor: حالها العجيبة في سرعة تقضيها وذهاب نعيمها بعد إقبالها واغترار الناس بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r2.claim: Rain mingles and interweaves plants eaten by people and livestock, including crops, vegetables, and pasture.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r2.anchor: فاشتبك بسببه حتى خالط بعضه بعضا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r3.claim: The earth takes on its beauty and becomes decorated in varied colors like a bride wearing fine garments and ornaments.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r3.anchor: { حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها } حسنها وبهجتها. { وازينت } تزينت بأصناف النبات وأشكالها وألوانها المختلفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r4.claim: Several forms explain izzayyanat: assimilation from tazayyanat, an unaltered ifta'ala form, or a form meaning it became adorned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r4.anchor: { وازينت } أصله تزينت فأدغم وقد قرىء على الأصل { وازينت } على أفعلت من غير إعلال

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r5.claim: The owners think they can harvest the crop; God's command strikes it with what it needs, leaving it cut down as though it had never flourished.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r5.anchor: { وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها } متمكنون من حصدها ورفع غلتها. { أتاها أمرنا } ضرب زرعها ما يحتاجه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r6.claim: The omitted noun in 'as though it had not flourished' is the crop, and the omission in both places intensifies the image; one reading uses the original ya form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r6.anchor: { كأن لم تغن } كأن لم يغن زرعها أي لم يلبث، والمضاف محذوف في الموضعين

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r7.claim: The comparison is a composite image of flourishing vegetation suddenly becoming debris, not a comparison with the rain itself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r7.anchor: والممثل به مضمون الحكاية وهو زوال خضرة النبات فجأة وذهابه حطاما

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r8.claim: God explains the signs for people who reflect, since they are the ones who benefit from them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:24/r8.anchor: { كذلك نفصل الآيت لقوم يتفكرون } فإنهم المنتفعون به.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r1.claim: Against people who imagine worldly life continues forever, the verse confines its likeness to fleeting vegetation, affirming resurrection and warning against oppression and unjust pride.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r1.anchor: وكانوا ينكرونه ويعتقدون بقاء الدنيا وأنها إنما هي أرحام تدفع وأرض تبلغ دائما بلا انقضاء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r2.claim: The opening إنما is a restrictive contrast: worldly enjoyment ends quickly after reaching its peak.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r2.anchor: { إنما } فهو قصر قلب { مثل الحياة الدنيا } التي تتنافسون فيها في سرعة انقضائها وانقراض نعيمها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r3.claim: Rain from heaven makes vegetation flourish throughout the earth, including grain, fruits, and herbs eaten by people and livestock; the imagery also points to resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r3.anchor: فشبهه بأمر النبات وانه قليل يبلغ منتهاه فتصبح الأرض منه بلاقع بعد ذلك الاخضرار والينوع

BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r4.claim: The earth takes on visible and hidden beauty from its plants; its owners strongly imagine they can harvest its produce, unaware of what comes next.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r4.anchor: أخذت الأرض } أي التي لها أهلية النبات { زخرفها وازينت } بأنواع ذلك النبات زينة منها الجلي ومنها الخفي

BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r5.claim: God's command, such as extreme cold or heat by night or day, can turn the flourishing crop into harvested remnants, as if it had never been beautiful or abundant.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r5.anchor: { أتاها أمرنا } اي الذي لا يرد من البرد أو الحر المفرطين

BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r6.claim: The vanished crop illustrates the world's rapid loss of prosperity; God details signs like this for people who think, and the author defines parable, intermixture, and adornment.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p432/r6.anchor: فكان حال الدنيا في سرعة انقضائها وانقراض نعيمها بعد عظيم إقباله كحال نبات الأرض

DURR-FULL:v4p353/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p353/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p353/r9.claim: Water makes every kind of plant grow: grains and other crops, legumes, and fruits for people, and grass and pasture for livestock.
DURR-FULL:v4p353/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {فاختلط به نبات الأرض} قال: اختلط فنبت بالماء كل لون

DURR-FULL:v4p354/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r1.claim: Qatada glosses “adorned” as sprouted and beautified, and “as if it had not flourished yesterday” as if it had never lived or enjoyed prosperity.
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {وازينت} قال: أنبتت وحسنت وفي قوله {كأن لم تغن بالأمس} قال: كأن لم تعش

DURR-FULL:v4p354/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب، ابن عباس، مروان بن الحكم
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r2.claim: Ubayy, Ibn Abbas, and Marwan are reported to read an added phrase: God would not destroy its people except for their sins.
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r2.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب وابن عباس ومروان بن الحكم أنهم كانوا يقرأون {وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها}

DURR-FULL:v4p354/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r3.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r3.claim: Abu Salama reports Ubayy's reading with the added statement that the land was destroyed only for its people's sins.
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r3.anchor: عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن قال في قراءة أبي كأن لم تغن بالأمس وما أهلكناها إلا بذنوب أهلها

DURR-FULL:v4p354/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r4.speaker: أبو مجلز
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r4.claim: Abu Majliz says a saying was written beside the verse about wealth: a person with two valleys wants a third, is filled only by dust, and God accepts whoever repents; the saying was later erased.
DURR-FULL:v4p354/r4.anchor: عن أبي مجلز رضي الله عنه قال: مكتوب في سورة يونس عليه السلام إلى جنب هذه الآية {حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها}

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says this is a good parable, like God's other parables, specially illustrating what believers and unbelievers are given.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : ضرب الله مثلا حسنا وكل امثاله حسن وهو مثل خص به الله المؤمن والكافر فيما اوتيا .

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra says every drop of rain descends in a measured amount.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r2.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب ان أبا هريرة قال : مانزل قطر الا بميزان

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r3.claim: Ikrima says God sends water from the seventh heaven and a raindrop rests on a cloud like a camel.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : ينزل الله الماء من السماء السابعة فتسع القطرة منه على السحابة مثل البعير

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r4.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r4.claim: Ata says the earth's plants mix with the rainwater and grow in many colors.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r4.anchor: اما اختلط به نبات الأرض فاختلط فنبت بالماء من كل لون

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says the livestock mentioned are grazing animals.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r5.anchor: عن السدى الانعام قال : والانعام : الراعية

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r6.claim: Mujahid says he understood زخرف as gold after reading Abdullah's recitation, a house of gold; the cited wording occurs at 17:93.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r6.anchor: عن الحكم عن مجاهد قال : ماكنت ادري ماالزخرف حتى قرات قراءه عبدالله ' أو يكون لك بيت من ذهب

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r7.claim: Qatada glosses the earth's becoming adorned as growing and becoming beautiful.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r7.anchor: عن قتادة وازينت قال : انبتت وحسنت

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r8.claim: Qatada warns that the world soon casts off and abandons the person attached to it, even when its beauty most delights him.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r8.anchor: عن قتادة وظن اهلها انهم قادرون عليها اتاها امرنا ليلا ونهارا اي والله لمن تشبث بالدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r9.claim: Qatada says the earth became as though it had not enjoyed its former flourishing.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1940/r9.anchor: عن قتادة كان لم تغن بالامس قال : كان لم تنعم بالامس

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r1.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the earth's former flourishing as its adornment.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r1.anchor: عن السدى كان لم تغن بالامس بزينتها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says God makes the signs clear by explaining them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r2.anchor: عن السدى كذلك نفصل اما نفصل : فنبين

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says reflection means considering the world's passing and the Hereafter's arrival and permanence.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : يتفكرون يعني : في زوال الدنيا وفنائها واقبال الاخرة وبقائها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r4.claim: Hasan says reflection shows that the world is an abode of trial and then extinction, while the Hereafter is an abode of recompense and enduring life.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r4.anchor: شهدت الحسن وقرا هذا الاية : يتفكرون قال : هو والله لمن تفكر فيها يعلم ان الدنيا دار بلاء

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r5.claim: Qatada says God singled out this parable for reflection and urges people to understand it, citing 29:43 about parables grasped by the learned.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r5.anchor: عن قتادة لقوم يتفكرون قال : هذا مثل خص به الله فاعقلوا عن الله امثاله

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r6.claim: Mujahid also glosses reflecting as obeying.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1942/r6.anchor: عن الثوري قال : قال مجاهد يتفكرون : يطيعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r1.claim: The parable explains worldly enjoyment in 10:23: it lasts briefly, like crops that flourish and then are harvested; the analogy compares two composite scenes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية تتنزل منزلة البيان لجملة { متاع الحياة الدنيا } ( يونس : 23 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r2.claim: The restrictive form stresses how quickly worldly life ends and reverses the audience's assumed belief that its beauty will last.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r2.anchor: وصيغة القصر لتأكيد المقصود من التشبيه وهو سرعة الانقضاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r3.claim: The whole of worldly life is compared to flourishing vegetation in its rapid passing and loss of beauty after its peak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r3.anchor: شبهت حالة الحياة في سرعة تقضيها وزوال نعيمها بعد البهجة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r4.claim: Rain corresponds to the beginning of life in childhood, when hopes of comfort and freshness first arise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p141#2/r4.anchor: شبه به ابتداء أطوار الحياة من وقت الصبا إذ ليس ثمة سوى الأمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r1.claim: The plant mixing with water represents the first flourishing of life; the فاء signals how quickly vegetation and life's growth appear, and mixing means proximity before the water dries.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r1.anchor: ولذلك عطف بفاء التعقيب للإيذان بسرعة ظهور النبات عقب المطر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r2.claim: Human and animal food plants represent pleasures enjoyed by people and animals; lofty ambitions resemble human food, low ambitions cattle fodder, as in 47:12.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r2.anchor: منه أصناف يأكلها الناس من الخضروات والبقول ، وأصناف تأكلها الأنعام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r3.claim: The crop's full ornament and growth represents the peak of worldly benefit, abundance, and absorption in pleasure while people forget its end; compare 10:22.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r3.anchor: وهو غاية شبه بها بلوغ الانتفاع بخيرات الدنيا إلى أقصاه ونضوجه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r4.claim: God's أمر is His decree and creation; its arrival means calamities that rapidly dry and destroy the land, while حتى compresses many stages between life's beginning and end.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p142/r4.anchor: وأمر الله : تقديره وتكوينه . وإتيانه : إصابة تلك الأرض بالجوائح المعجلة لها باليبس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r1.claim: Night or day leaves every time possible for the sudden end, so no appointed interval gives people security.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r1.anchor: ترديد في الوقت لإثارة التوقع من إمكان زوال نضارة الحياة في جميع الأزمنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r2.claim: Zukhruf means gold and by extension adornment; the land is personified as a woman taking fine clothes and jewelry, supported by 7:31 and Bashshar's poem.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r2.anchor: وإطلاق أخذ الأرض زخرفها على حصول الزينة فيها استعارة مكنية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r3.speaker: بشار بن برد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r3.claim: Bashshar's poem uses the verb خذي for taking ornate clothes and colors, supporting the image of taking adornment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r3.anchor: وقال بشار بن برد : وخذي ملابس زينة ومصبغات وهي أفخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r4.claim: ازينت derives from تزينت, with ت changed to ز and assimilated, and a connecting hamza added for pronunciation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r4.anchor: و { ازينت } أصله تزينت فقلبت التاء زايا ؛ لتدغم في الزاي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r5.claim: The sudden command and harvest signal total destruction and threaten unbelievers; the detail that people think they control the land identifies them as the target, like 6:44.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r5.anchor: إشارة لإرادة الاستئصال فهو ينذر بالتهديد للكافرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r6.claim: Being able to control the land metaphorically means continuing to benefit from it and gather its produce.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r6.anchor: أنهم مستمرون على الانتفاع بها محصلون لثمراتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r7.claim: حصيد means harvested crop; calling the land harvested is a rational metaphor for its plants, while لم تغن means it was not inhabited or cultivated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p143/r7.anchor: والحصيد : المحصود ، وهو الزرع المقطوع من منابته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r1.claim: The باء in بالأمس marks time; أمس means any past period here, as غد and يوم can mean the future and present, illustrated by Zuhayr's verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r1.anchor: والمراد بالأمس في الآية مطلق الزمن الذي مضى لأن أمس يستعمل بمعنى ما مضى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r2.speaker: زهير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r2.claim: Zuhayr's verse contrasts knowledge of today and yesterday with ignorance of tomorrow, supporting أمس as past time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r2.anchor: وجمعها قول زهير : وأعلم علم اليوم والأمسس قبله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r3.claim: The closing statement about explaining signs generalizes to proofs of God's knowledge, power, and precision; this parable is one such sign and resembles 6:55.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r3.anchor: مثل هذا التفصيل نفصل أي نبين الدلالات كلها الدالة على عموم العلم والقدرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r4.claim: The لام in لقوم is purposive; reflection means careful consideration, and the passage hints that those who gain no benefit are not reflective people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p144/r4.anchor: والتفكر : التأمل والنظر ، وهو تفعل مشتق من الفكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r1.claim: The adorned, boasting worldly life of wealth and children, which ends in extinction, is likened to rain that produces mixed growth.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r2.speaker: فرقة من القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r2.claim: Some readers stop at فاختلط, taking it to mean that water mixed with earth, then resume with نبات الأرض as a new clause with a fronted predicate; به can refer to water or to the implied mixing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r2.anchor: ثم استأنف به نبات الأرض على الابتداء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r3.claim: Another group connects نبات as the subject of اختلط: plants mixed with one another because of the water.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r4.claim: What people eat means crops, trees, and similar growth; what livestock eat means all grazing herbage.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r5.claim: أخذت الأرض is a common idiom, as in 7:31; زخرف means colorful adornment and can also mean gold, from which it is made.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r5.anchor: التزين بالألوان، وقد يجيء الزخرف بمعنى الذهب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r6.speaker: مروان بن الحكم وأبو جعفر والسبعة وشيبة ومجاهد والجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r6.claim: They read وازينت, from تزينت with tāʾ assimilated and a connecting alif; Ibn Masud, al-A'mash, and Ubay read the unassimilated وتزينت.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r6.anchor: وقرأ مروان بن الحكم وأبو جعفر والسبعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r7.speaker: الحسن وأبو العالية والشعبي وقتادة ونصر بن عاصم وعيسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r7.claim: They read وأزينت as though the land had put on its adornment, analogous to أحصد الزرع; other recitations include وا زيانت, وازيأنت, and وازاينت, all meaning that its adornment appeared, with a poet's line cited for one form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو العالية والشعبي وقتادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r8.claim: وظن أهلها is read in its ordinary sense; عليها refers to the earth and its blessings and plants. The whole worldly-life scene is compared to the described field.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r8.anchor: والضمير في عليها عائد على الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r9.claim: حتى marks the endpoint and begins a clause with إذا; the description extends through the people's belief that they control the land, after which the outcome begins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r9.anchor: وحتى غاية وهي حرف ابتداء لدخولها على إذا ومعناها متصل إلى قوله قادرون عليها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r10.claim: The arriving أمر is a destructive force such as wind, cold, or simoom; specifying night or day warns that danger and loss of security can come at any time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r10.anchor: والأمر الآتي واحد الأمور كالريح والصر والسموم ونحو ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r11.claim: حصيد is an active-form word with passive meaning, describing ruined vegetation whether harvested or destroyed by blight, as though calamity cut it down early.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p114/r11.anchor: عن التالف الهالك من النبات وإن لم يهلك بحصاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r1.claim: تغن means to flourish or thrive; Qatada reads يغن with yāʾ referring to the ruined crop, and Marwan reads كأن لم تتغن. المغاني means inhabited dwellings, supported by a poetic example.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r1.anchor: قرأ قتادة «يغن» بالياء من تحت يعني الحصيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r2.claim: Ubay's codex adds that the land would not have been destroyed except for its people's sins; this is transmitted by Ibn Abbas, with another version naming God as the subject.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r2.anchor: مصحف أبي بن كعب «كأن لم تغن بالأمس وما كنا لنهلكها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda reads لقوم يتذكرون in place of يتفكرون.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r4.claim: The parable warns against being deluded by worldly life, which is exposed to destruction through death or other calamities; mentioning reflective people honors their rank and invites others to compete for it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p115/r4.anchor: إذ هي معرضة للتلف وأن يصيبها

SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r1.claim: The passage compares worldly life with the growth of the earth's plants and explains the likeness through the described sequence.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r1.anchor: هذه الجملة سيقت لتشبيه الدنيا بنبات الأرض، وقد شرح الله تعالى وجه التشبيه بما ذكر.

SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls it a compound simile: worldly delight quickly vanishes after flourishing like luxuriant vegetation that dries into debris.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وهذا من/ التشبيه المركب، شبهت حال الدنيا في سرعة تقضيها

SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r3.claim: A compound simile may have two composite sides; Bashshar ibn Burd's image of falling stars and swords illustrates this type.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24/r3.anchor: كقول بشار بن برد: 2578 كان مثار النقع فوق رؤوسنا وأسيافنا

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r1.claim: كماء is the predicate, أنزلناه is an adjective of ماء, and من السماء depends on أنزلناه; making it a circumstantial phrase from the object pronoun is weak.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: { كمآء } هو خبر المبتدأ، و " أنزلناه " صفة ل " ماء "

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the ba in فاختلط به as causal: vegetation mingled because of the water.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فاشتبك بسببه حتى خالط بعضه بعضا "

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the vegetation itself is the subject of فاختلط, and its parts mingle because of the water.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " وصلت فرقة " النبات "

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r4.claim: Another analysis makes the ba one of accompaniment: water accompanies the vegetation as its nourishment.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r4.anchor: والثاني: أنها للمصاحبة بمعنى أن الماء يجري مجرى الغذاء له فهو مصاحبه.

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports a proposed pause after فاختلط, with the pronoun in به referring either to water or to the mixing implied by the verb.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r5.anchor: والضمير في " به " على هذا يجوز عوده على الماء، وأن يعود على الاختلاط الذي تضمنه الفعل، قاله ابن عطية.

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r6.claim: Al-Shaykh rejects that pause as breaking connected, eloquent syntax and turning the passage into a riddle.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#2/r6.anchor: قال الشيخ: " الوقف على قوله: " فاختلط " لا يجوز، وخاصة في القرآن لأنه تفكيك للكلام المتصل الصحيح

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r1.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r1.claim: Al-Hawfi attaches مما يأكل to اختلط.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنه متعلق ب " اختلط " وبه قال الحوفي.

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats مما يأكل as a circumstantial phrase from النبات; the author calls this apparent and supplies an omitted كائنا or مستقرا.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه حال من " النبات " وبه قال أبو البقاء، وهو الظاهر

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r3.claim: من could instead mark the kind of vegetation people and livestock eat.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r3.anchor: ولو قيل " من " لبيان الجنس لجاز.

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r4.claim: حتى needs a durative event to reach its endpoint; اختلط is too brief, so either plant growth is omitted or اختلط means continued mixing.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r4.anchor: والفعل الذي قبلها وهو " اختلط " لا يصلح أن يكون مغيا لقصر زمنه.

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r5.claim: The construction of إذا after حتى was discussed earlier.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r5.anchor: و " إذا " بعد " حتى " هذه تقدم التنبيه عليها.

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r6.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r6.claim: The majority read ازينت with hamzat al-wasl and a doubled zay and yā; its underlying form is وتزينت, assimilated for pronunciation.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r6.anchor: قرأ الجمهور " ازينت " بوصل الهمزة وتشديد الزاي والياء، والأصل

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب وعبد الله وزيد بن علي والأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r7.claim: These readers preserve the underlying form وتزينت.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب وعبد الله وزيد بن علي والأعمش " وتزينت " على تفعلت

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r8.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص والسلمي وابن يعمر والحسن والشعبي وأبو العالية ونصر بن عاصم وابن هرمز وعيسى الثقفي
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r8.claim: They read وأزينت as an afʿala form meaning that the earth became adorned; the expected alif shift is irregularly absent, like أغيمت and استحوذ.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r8.anchor: وقرأ سعد ابن أبي وقاص والسلمي وابن يعمر والحسن والشعبي وأبو العالية ونصر بن عاصم

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r9.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي وفرقة
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r9.claim: They read وازيأنت, with hamza replacing the alif in an underlying وازيانت to avoid adjacent quiescent sounds; the line احمأرت is cited as a parallel.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#3/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو عثمان النهدي وعزاه ابن عطية لفرقة غير معينة " وازيأنت " بهمزة وصل

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r1.claim: أهلها means the people of the plants; أتاها governs إذا, while its pronoun may refer to adornment or produce, with no ellipsis in the latter reading.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r1.anchor: وقوله: { أهلهآ } ، أي: أهل نباتها. و " أتاها " هو جواب " إذا "

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r2.claim: ليلا ونهارا may modify the arrival or the command; جعل is causative and حصيد is a passive participle that need not take feminine marking.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r2.anchor: و " ليلا ونهارا " ظرفان للإتيان أو للأمر. والجعل هنا تصيير. وحصيد: فعيل بمعنى مفعول

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r3.claim: كأن لم تغن can be a circumstantial clause from the first object of جعلناها or an independent answer to an implied question.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r3.anchor: قوله: { كأن لم تغن } هذه الجملة يجوز أن تكون حالا من مفعول " جعلناها " الأول

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r4.speaker: مروان بن الحكم
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r4.claim: Marwan reads تتغن with two tāʾs, as in al-Aʿsha's line; the form means remaining or dwelling.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r4.anchor: وقرأ مروان ابن الحكم " تتغن " بتاءين بزنة تنفعل

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r5.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada read لم يغن with a masculine pronoun, most plausibly returning to حصيد; alternatives are the adornment or the implied plant/crop.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة { كأن لم يغن } بياء الغيبة، وفي هذا الضمير ثلاثة أوجه، أجودها

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r6.claim: بالأمس means the past generally, not specifically the day before today, as in Zuhayr's cited line; this form is declinable unlike the fixed word for yesterday.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r6.anchor: و " بالأمس " المراد به الزمن الماضي لا اليوم الذي قبل يومك

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r7.speaker: أشياخ عوف بن أبي جميلة
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r7.claim: They read وازيأنت from the same proposed original; Ibn Atiyya attributes this reading to Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, while another reading وازاينت assimilates تزاينت.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#4/r7.anchor: وقرأ أشياخ عوف ابن أبي جميلة: " وازيأنت " بالأصل المشار إليه

SAMIN-DURR:10:24#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#5/r1.claim: كذلك نفصل describes a verbal noun omitted from the syntax: just as the explanation was given before, signs will be explained later.
SAMIN-DURR:10:24#5/r1.anchor: وقوله: { كذلك نفصل } نعت مصدر محذوف، أي: مثل هذا التفصيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r1.claim: The fading worldly life is compared to rain that mixes with plants, making abundant crops for people and pasture for animals.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r1.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله للدنيا الفانية فشببها بمطر نزل من السماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r2.claim: The earth's ornament is its greenery; the word originally means gold and came to denote decorated engraving, blossoms, flowers, and whatever is adorned.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة زينتها بالنبات وأصل الزخرف الذهب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r3.claim: Zakhraf means the perfection of a thing's beauty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج الزخرف كمال حسن الشيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r4.claim: Most readers use the geminated form wazzayyanat, meaning “became adorned” through assimilation; Sa'd, Abu Abd al-Rahman, al-Hasan, and Ibn Ya'mar use a lighter form meaning “came with its adornment,” while Ubayy and Ibn Masud read “and adorned itself.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p21/r4.anchor: قرأه الجمهور وازينت بالتشديد وقرأ سعد ابن أبي وقاص وأبو عبد الرحمن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r1.claim: Rain-grown crops and fruits for people and pasture for animals portray worldly life's beauty, brief flourishing, and swift disappearance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r1.anchor: تعالى مثلا لزهرة الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وسرعة انقضائها وزوالها، بالنبات الذي أخرجه الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r2.claim: The earth takes its fading ornament, blooms in varied forms and colors, and its owners expect to harvest; then a sudden command by night or day leaves it dry and destroyed, as if never beautiful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r2.anchor: أتاها أمرنا ليلا أو نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r3.claim: Qatada explains the phrase about the land seeming never to have flourished as meaning it had never enjoyed prosperity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: {كأن لم تغن} كأن لم تنعم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r4.claim: Worldly affairs after their disappearance seem never to have existed; a person given the greatest worldly bliss forgets it after one dip in Hell, and the most miserable forgets suffering after one dip in delight.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r4.anchor: يؤتى بأنعم أهل الدنيا، فيغمس في النار غمسة ثم يقال له: هل رأيت خيرا قط

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r5.claim: The parable urges reflection on the world's rapid passing despite people's confidence; God also compares worldly life to vegetation elsewhere.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260/r5.anchor: فيعتبرون بهذا المثل في زوال الدنيا من أهلها سريعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p260#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Ubayy ibn Kaʿb taught a reading adding that God would not destroy the land except for its people's sins; Ibn Kathir calls it unusual and likely an explanatory addition.

JISHUMI:v5p3348/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r7.claim: The common reading has وازينت with yāʾ and a doubled zāy; al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī read وازيانت, on the pattern of احمارت.
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r7.anchor: وعن الضحاك وأبي عثمان النهدي: وازيانت، على وزن: واحمارت

JISHUMI:v5p3348/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r8.speaker: أبو العالية والحسن والشعبي والأعرج
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r8.claim: They read وأزينت with a hamza and still zāy, on the pattern of أفعلت.
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r8.anchor: عن أبي العالية والحسن والشعبي والأعرج: [وأزينت على وزن أفعلت]

JISHUMI:v5p3348/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r9.claim: The common reading has كأن لم تغن with feminine tāʾ referring to earth; Qatāda reads it with yāʾ referring to the earth's adornment.
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r9.anchor: [كأن لم تغن] بالتاء لتأنيث الأرض، وعن قتادة بالياء

JISHUMI:v5p3348/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r10.claim: Mathal is a familiar saying comparing a later situation to an earlier one, or a descriptive attribute; with kasra, mithl means counterpart, and the related forms include punishment, example, and the best among a people.
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r10.anchor: المثل: قول سائر يشبه به حال الثاني بحال الأول، وجمعه: أمثال، والمثل: الصفة

JISHUMI:v5p3348/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r11.claim: Ikhtilāṭ is the reciprocal form of mixing and means things interpenetrating one another.
JISHUMI:v5p3348/r11.anchor: والاختلاط: افتعال من الخلط، وهو تداخل الأشياء بعضها في بعض

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r1.claim: Hasidan can mean gone away or dried out.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r2.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the land seemed never to have been inhabited yesterday.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r2.anchor: كأن لم تعمر بالأمس , قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r3.claim: Qatada says the land seemed never to have lived yesterday; he cites Labid's verse about living in a place after the battle of Dahis.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r3.anchor: كأنه لم تعش بالأمس , قاله قتادة , ومنه قول لبيد :

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r4.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r4.claim: Ali ibn Isa says the land seemed not to have stood or remained in the place yesterday.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r4.anchor: كأن لم تقم بالأمس , ومن قولهم غنى فلان بالمكان إذا أقام فيه , قاله علي بن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r5.claim: Qatada also interprets the phrase as if the land had not enjoyed prosperity yesterday.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p430/r5.anchor: كأن لم تنعم بالأمس , قاله قتادة أيضا .

MUQATIL:10:24-25/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:10:24-25/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:10:24-25/r1.claim: Worldly life resembles plants that flourish green and then dry up; rain produces fruits for people and vegetation for animals.
MUQATIL:10:24-25/r1.anchor: يقول: مثل الدنيا كمثل النبت بينا هو أخضر، إذا هو قد يبس، فكذلك الدنيا إذا جاءت الآخرة،

MUQATIL:10:24-25/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:10:24-25/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:10:24-25/r2.claim: When the earth is lush and its people think they control it, God's command suddenly makes it harvested and gone; worldly pleasure gives way to the hereafter.
MUQATIL:10:24-25/r2.anchor: { حتى إذآ أخذت الأرض زخرفها } ، يعني حسنها وزينتها، { وازينت } بالنبات وحسنت، { وظن أهلهآ } ، يعني وأيقن أهلها

MUQATIL:10:24-25/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:10:24-25/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:10:24-25/r3.claim: The signs are explained so people may reflect on God's wonders and lordship.
MUQATIL:10:24-25/r3.anchor: { نفصل الآيات } ، يعني نبين العلامات { لقوم يتفكرون } [آية: 24] في عجائب الله وربوبيته.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r1.claim: Rain from clouds makes the plants of earth intertwine; these include grains, fruits, and vegetables eaten by people and grass eaten by livestock.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ فاختلط به ﴾ بالماء ﴿ نبات الأرض ﴾ أى فاشتبك بسببه حتى خالط بعضه بعضا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r2.claim: When the earth takes on its vegetation's ornament and beautifies itself, the text personifies it like a bride wearing luxurious clothes of many colors; izzayyanat assimilates the tāʾ into zāy.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r2.anchor: وتزينت به وهو أصله وأدغمت التاء فى الزاى وهو كلام فصيح

NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r3.claim: The inhabitants think they control the crop and can gather its yield, but God's command strikes it by day or night and leaves it cut down as if it had never flourished; omitted possessives mean its crop.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r3.anchor: متمكنون من منفعتها محصلون لثمرتها رافعون لغلتها ﴿ أتاها أمرنا ﴾ عذابنا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r4.claim: Al-ams is an idiom for the recent past; the deletion in 'as if it had not flourished' supplies the crop as the subject.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r4.anchor: هو مثل فى الوقت القريب كأنه قيل كأن لم تغن آنفا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r5.claim: The compound simile portrays worldly life rapidly ending after its peak, like lush, dense vegetation drying away; it teaches that worldly pleasure is mixed with bitterness.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r5.anchor: وهذا من التشبيه المركب شبهت حال الدنيا فى سرعة تقضيها وانقراض نعيمها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r6.claim: The source quotes an unattributed line comparing life to a cup of old wine, clear at first and turbid at the end.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r7.claim: An extended allegory contrasts wholesome clay yielding intimacy, piety, generosity, love, and spiritual gardens with corrupt clay producing shirk, greed, harm, and frivolity; death harvests the crop before resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r7.anchor: فالطينة الطيبة تنبت بساتين الانس ورياحين الرحوح وزهرة الزهد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r8.claim: Water benefits in small amounts and destroys in excess; worldly wealth likewise demands leaving surplus and taking provisions, while acquiring it entails missteps and hoarding destroys its owner.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r8.anchor: وكذلك حال الدنيا كالماء ينفع قليله ويهلك كثيره ولا بد من ترك مازاد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r9.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying zakat is the bridge of Islam; the allegory likens zakat to a bridge over the river of wealth, maintained by prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r9.anchor: وعن هذا قال عليه السلام الزكاة قنطرة الإسلام

NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r10.claim: Wealth favors base people rather than noble ones and gathers through a miser's toil like water collected in lowlands behind a dam; it eventually vanishes like water in the hand.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p124#2/r10.anchor: وكذالك المال لا يجتمع إلا بكد البخيل كما أن الماء لا يجتمع إلا بسد المسيل

ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r1.claim: Zakhraf is the full beauty of a thing; zayyanat is a geminated reading for ‘adorned,’ with tāʾ assimilated into zāy.

ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r2.claim: The lighter reading azyanat uses form IV, meaning the land produced its adornment.
ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r2.anchor: بالتخفيف فهو على أفعلت أي جاءت بالزينة

ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r3.claim: He prefers the geminated zayyanat as better Arabic; the lighter form would more naturally be azānat.
ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r3.anchor: بالتشديد أجود في العربية، لأن أزينت الأجود فيه

ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p14/r4.claim: The landowners thought they could benefit from or make use of the harvest.

ZAJJAJ:v3p15/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p15/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p15/r1.claim: Taghna means ‘be inhabited’; maghānī are dwellings, and the phrase ‘we dwelt in a place’ uses the same root.
ZAJJAJ:v3p15/r1.anchor: أي كأن لم تعمر بالأمس، والمغاني المنازل

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r1.claim: The parable portrays worldly life as fleeting, vanishing, and of little value or pleasure; its condition resembles water from the sky, with the comparison particle in a nominative construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r1.anchor: أي صفة الحياة الدنيا في فنائها وزوالها وقلة خطرها والملاذ بها كماء

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r2.claim: The phrase ‘which We sent down from heaven’ describes the water; Qurtubi promises fuller treatment of this comparison in al-Kahf.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r3.speaker: نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r3.claim: Nafi‘ pauses after ‘it mixed’: water mixes into the earth, then the vegetation of the earth grows by that water; vegetation is the subject of the next clause.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r3.anchor: روي عن نافع أنه وقف على «فاختلط» أي فاختلط الماء بالأرض،

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r4.claim: Without Nafi‘’s pause, the vegetation is the subject of ‘mixed’: it mixes with the rain, drinks it, and becomes moist, beautiful, and green; ikhtilat means interpenetration.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r4.anchor: وعلى مذهب من لم يقف على «فاختلط» مرفوع باختلط أي اختلط النبات بالمطر،

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r5.claim: People eat grain, fruit, and vegetables from the vegetation, while livestock eat pasture, straw, and barley.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى: { مما يأكل الناس } من الحبوب والثمار والبقول. { والأنعام } من الكلإ والتبن والشعير.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r6.claim: The earth takes its full beauty and adornment, hence gold is called ornament; ‘and it was adorned’ derives from tazayyanat with assimilation and a joining hamza.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r6.anchor: والزخرف كمال حسن الشيء ومنه قيل للذهب: زخرف.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r7.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud and Ubayy read the unassimilated original form, ‘and it adorns itself.’
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب «وتزينت» على الأصل.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r8.speaker: الحسن والأعرج وأبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r8.claim: Al-Hasan, al-A‘raj, and Abu al-A‘liya read ‘and it brought forth its adornment,’ using the verb in its original form.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعرج وأبو العالية «وأزينت» أي أتت بالزينة عليها،

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r9.speaker: عوف بن أبي جميلة الأعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r9.claim: ‘Awf ibn Abi Jamilah says his elders read the form waziyānat; al-Muqaddami transmits wazāyanat, from tazāyanat with assimilation.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r9.anchor: وقال عوف بن أبي جميلة الأعرابي: قرأ أشياخنا «وازيانت»

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r10.speaker: الشعبي وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r10.claim: Al-Sha‘bi and Qatada read the verb as ‘azayyanat,’ on the af‘alat pattern.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r11.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r11.claim: Abu Uthman al-Nahdi transmits three additional forms: az-zayyanat, zayānat, and azya’ant with hamza.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو عثمان النهدي «وازينت» مثل افعلت،

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r12.claim: ‘Its people thought they had power over it’ means they were certain they could harvest and benefit from it; the pronoun may refer to the earth, its yield, or its adornment.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r12.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وظن أهلها } أي أيقن. { أنهم قادرون عليها } أي على حصادها والانتفاع بها

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r13.claim: God’s command arriving means either His punishment or His order that the land be destroyed; night and day are temporal adverbs.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r14.claim: ‘Harvested’ means cut down with nothing remaining; it is masculine because fa‘il has the sense of maf‘ul, and Abu Ubayda defines it as uprooted completely.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r14.anchor: ولم يؤنث لأنه فعيل بمعنى مفعول

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r15.claim: ‘As though it had not flourished yesterday’ comes from ghaniya, to reside and inhabit; al-maghani are inhabited homes, while Qatada glosses it as not having enjoyed prosperity.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24/r15.anchor: { كأن لم تغن بالأمس } أي لم تكن عامرة من غني إذا أقام فيه وعمره.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r1.claim: Labid’s line supplies a linguistic example for ghaniya, ‘to inhabit’ or dwell in a place.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r2.speaker: قراءة العامة
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r2.claim: The common reading uses the feminine verb taghn because its grammatical subject is the earth.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r3.claim: Qatada reads yaghnu with yā’, referring to the adornment; the crop’s sudden destruction illustrates the same fate of worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ قتادة «يغن» بالياء، يذهب به إلى الزخرف

QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r4.claim: To detail the signs means to make them clear for people who reflect on God’s signs.
QURTUBI-FULL:10:24#2/r4.anchor: أي نبينها. { لقوم يتفكرون } في آيات الله.

RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r1.claim: After warning that wrongdoing returns upon its perpetrators (10:23), the verse likens worldly attachment to a luxuriant garden that can be ruined suddenly, leaving its owner heartbroken.
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r1.anchor: أتبعه بهذا المثل العجيب الذي ضربه لمن يبغي في الأرض ويغتر بالدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r2.claim: The phrase about vegetation mixing with the rain may mean varied plants sprout because of the rain, or that rain revives young growth until it becomes beautiful and full.
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r2.anchor: أن يكون المعنى فاختلط به نبات الأرض بسبب هذا الماء النازل من السماء

RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r3.claim: The earth taking its adornment is compared to a bride dressed in fine garments and decorated in many colors; the owner's hopes rise as the garden flourishes.
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r3.anchor: فجعلت الأرض آخذة زخرفها على التشبيه بالعروس إذا لبست الثياب الفاخرة

RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r4.claim: A sudden frost, wind, or flood can destroy the flourishing orchard by night or day, just as the loss of worldly pleasures makes the person attached to them grieve.
RAZI-FULL:v17p59/r4.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى يرسل على هذا البستان العجيب آفة عظيمة دفعة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r1.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r1.claim: One analogy is that people most attached to worldly life often die just when hope of enjoying it is greatest, like a crop ruined at its peak; 6:44 gives a parallel.
RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r1.anchor: أن عاقبة هذه الحياة الدنيا التي ينفقها المرء في باب الدنيا كعاقبة هذا النبات

RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r2.claim: A second analogy is that the worldly lover, like the doomed crop, reaches no praiseworthy outcome.
RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r2.anchor: في التشبيه أنه تعالى بين أنه كما لم يحصل لذلك الزرع عاقبة تحمد

RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r3.claim: A third analogy is that worldly strivers' efforts are rendered void, like the farmer's labor when disaster destroys the crop; 25:23 is cited.
RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r3.anchor: مثل قوله سبحانه : { وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا }

RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v17p59#2/r4.claim: A fourth analogy is the farmer's grief after costly labor becomes the cause of future misery, like the person whose effort for worldly gain becomes a source of afterlife suffering.
